note: Paraphrased from the GURPS 4e Basic Set and Magic for the rules tab in the builder. Not book text. Keys are library names; a skill key may add a specialization, e.g. "Thrown Weapon (Knife)", which wins over the plain name. Penalties are in GURPS levels. Run node tools/build_desc.mjs after editing.

skills.Knife: Fighting with any rigid, hilted blade under a foot long, from a pocketknife to a bowie knife. The blade is too small to parry well: -1 to Parry.
skills.Thrown Weapon: Throwing one type of weapon accurately. Each type is its own specialization: axe/mace, dart, harpoon, knife, shuriken, spear or stick.
skills.Thrown Weapon (Knife): Throwing any kind of knife. The other Thrown Weapon specializations (axe/mace, dart, harpoon, shuriken, spear, stick) are separate skills.
skills.Stealth: Hiding and moving quietly. A success hides you anywhere short of a bare room, keeps your movement silent, or lets you follow someone unseen (in a crowd, use Shadowing). Against a guard who is watching for intruders, the GM rolls a Quick Contest of your Stealth against the guard's Perception. Stalking animals: a roll and about 30 minutes gets you within 30 yards; a second roll at -5 gets you within 15. Penalties: your encumbrance level; -5 with no natural cover (+3 or more with plenty of it); -5 to stay silent while moving faster than Move 1; -5 against keen noses such as dogs.
skills.Climbing: Climbing cliffs, walls, trees and buildings (climbing rules on p. B349). Your encumbrance level is a penalty. Flexibility gives +3, Double-Jointed +5, Perfect Balance +1, Brachiator +2.
skills.Acrobatics: Gymnastic stunts, rolls, falls and balancing; each stunt is a separate roll at a penalty the GM sets. It can replace DX for jumping, rolling or keeping your feet, allows an Acrobatic Dodge in combat (p. B375), and a success takes five yards off the distance of a fall. Perfect Balance gives +1.
skills.Lockpicking: Opening a lock without its key or combination. An attempt takes a minute; a wide success is quicker (the book takes 5 seconds off per level of margin). A trap or alarm on the lock needs a separate Traps roll. -5 working by touch, such as in the dark; tools and inside information modify the roll.
skills.Poisons: Practical knowledge of poisons: spotting poisonous plants, extracting the poison, recognising a poison by taste or by its effects (+3 if you are the one poisoned), and knowing or making the antidote. Each task is a separate roll. Discriminatory Smell or Taste gives +4 when working by that sense.
skills.Fast-Talk: Talking people into snap decisions against their better judgement. Whenever a reaction roll applies, you may make an Influence roll with Fast-Talk instead (p. B359). The GM can ask for the story and adjust the roll for how plausible it is. Fast-Talk is for the quick con; Acting is for keeping up a deception over time. Voice gives +2, Low Empathy -3, Truthfulness -5.
skills.Observation: Watching a place, a group or your surroundings from a distance without showing that you are watching. A success picks up details nobody is hiding on purpose: cameras, sentry rotations, the size of a crowd. To spot something deliberately hidden, you must win a Quick Contest against the other side's Stealth, Shadowing or Camouflage; the GM rolls it in secret. Searching up close is Search; reading clues is Forensics.
skills.Occultism: Study of the supernatural: rituals, hauntings, mysticism, folk magic and psychic phenomena. It tells you what magic can do and how to deal with demons, but not how wizards cast spells; that is Thaumatology. The GM may require a specialty such as Demonology, Pneumatology (spirits) or Vampirology.
skills.Thaumatology: Academic magical theory. Mages add Magery to IQ for this skill, as for spells. Uses: researching new spells, identifying a spell you see cast, working out what a critical success or failure with magic did, and planning an enchantment. The better the roll, the more the GM tells you. Relating ritual or holy magic to wizardry is at -5.
skills.Hidden Lore: Knowledge that is lost, suppressed or ignored, and unknown to the public. Each body of knowledge is a specialization; Spirit Lore covers ghosts and other spirits, including their names and motives. No default. The GM may require it to be explained in the character's background and may tie improvement to finding sources. Somebody usually wants it kept secret, so revealing it can be dangerous.
skills.Brawling: Untrained unarmed fighting: punches, kicks at -2, natural weapons such as claws, teeth and horns, and the blackjack (a punch at +1 damage). At DX+2 or better it adds +1 per die to thrust damage for these attacks (not applied by the builder yet). Bare-hand parries: two per turn, one per hand, at -3 against weapons other than thrusts.
skills.Crossbow: Using any crossbow: pistol crossbows, prodds that shoot pellets or stones, repeating crossbows and compound crossbows.

spells.Death Vision: The subject sees a vivid vision of their own death, either a true one or one from a possible future. They are mentally stunned until they make an IQ roll to shake it off. It can also warn the subject of a deadly danger.
spells.Sense Spirit: Detects ghosts, spirits, undead and similar beings within the area. A good roll also gives a rough idea of what kind of being is there. When casting you can narrow it to one type or exclude one.
spells.Summon Spirit: Speak with a dead person's spirit. It answers one question, as far as it knew at death, and one more for each minute it stays. A friend of the caster resists at -5. Not knowing the full name is -5; time since death adds -1 (over a week) up to -6 (over 500 years). Halve the energy cost at the place of death or over the corpse, quarter it with both. On a failure the caster cannot summon that spirit again for a year. A critical failure brings a malign spirit that lies.
spells.Sense Foes: Tells whether the subject means harm, and how much. Cast over an area, it only reports that someone there is hostile, not who.
spells.Sense Emotion: Reads what a living subject feels right now, and how loyal they are to the caster (loyalty, p. B518).
spells.Fear: The subjects feel afraid. The caster gets +3 on reaction rolls where intimidation helps, and -3 where it backfires, such as loyalty rolls. Bravery counters it. It cannot be maintained.
spells.Turn Spirit: Drives one spirit the caster can see away from the caster at its full Move, until the spell ends or the caster loses sight of it. Meanwhile it cannot attack the caster by any means. A spirit possessing a body flees in that body. Each extra point of energy lowers the spirit's resistance by 1.
spells.Command Spirit: Charm (p. M139) for spirits: the spirit obeys, but may twist its orders the way a demon would. Each class of spirit (banshee, spectre and so on) is a separate spell; there is none for demons or elementals. Energy cost is 1 per 10 GURPS character points in the spirit, which is 1 per 100 Bell Curve points, and half that to maintain. Without a sheet, the book suggests 5 energy for a minor spirit and 10 for a formidable one.
